incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: PROD-DB-CONN-CASCADE — high error rate detected, automatic page fired (severity: P1). Affected services: write-api, async-processor. Alerts: Redis maxclients, Postgres connection_pool_busy. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incident/PROD-DB-CONN-CASCADE

alex (oncall): acked the page. i'm on it — starting triage.

maria (sre): seeing a large surge of `CONNECTIONS` in redis (maxclients at limit) and `FATAL: too many connections` in pg logs. latency to write-api ~ 1.8s -> 10s, ~15% 5xx.

sam (backend): confirming spikes correlate with a job fanout from async-processor, many short-lived DB connections. increasing pool_size on workers will not help instantly.

alex (oncall): first quick mitigation: enabling client-level backoff/rate-limit on router for write-api routes to reduce new spikes. rolling config now.

sam (backend): pushed a short-circuit to job enqueuer to collapse identical jobs for 60s, and added exponential backoff header for retries. will monitor.

maria (sre): Redis command: `redis-cli INFO clients` -> client_count: 11850, maxclients: 12000, evicted keys rising. pg pgbouncer stats show `cl_active` ~400, `sv_active` ~380 (close to max).

alex (oncall): temp mitigation 1/3: bumped Redis `maxclients` from 12000 -> 20000 on the replica pool to avoid abrupt rejects while we stabilize (change applied to non-primary replicas only). note: not persisting to conf yet.

jess (product): any customer-facing impact we should message? support-bot, can you surface recent support tickets?

support-bot: pulled 12 new high-latency incidents in last 30m. Top impacted orgs: Acme Co, BetaApps. Symptoms: delayed save, transaction timeouts. No widespread data loss reported.

maria (sre): temp mitigation 2/3: scaled read replicas + added one standby to offload read-heavy metrics queries that were hitting primary during the surge. Watching replication lag.

sam (backend): preparing a config change to switch app pools to pgbouncer in transaction pooling for the heaviest worker fleet. target: ~10-15min to roll. will coordinate with alex for safe rollout.

alex (oncall): alerted infra to increase pg connection limit on primary node (kernel limits ok) as temporary relief. infra confirmed they can allocate additional worker slots; making a small bump.

pagerduty: escalation: second level notified (oncall-sre-team).

lee (next-oncall): i'll take handoff after current plan completes. keep me posted with the state we want left for handoff.

alex (oncall): current state summary for handoff: router rate-limits engaged, redis maxclients temporarily increased, one extra read-replica added, job enqueuer backoff pushed, pgbouncer rollout queued (in-progress). No rollback planned yet.

maria (sre): monitoring: error rate down from 15% -> 5% over last 10m, but tail latency still elevated. replication lag negligible (0-2s). Redis evictions steady, but memory not the main issue.

sam (backend): pgbouncer rollouts started on async workers (gradual, 10% increments). early success on a canary host: connection reuse dropped new db connections by ~70%. continuing canary.

alex (oncall): added temporary circuit-breaker to async-processor to drop/enqueue non-critical jobs when DB queue depth > threshold. reduces immediate pressure.

jess (product): recommend messaging to affected customers: "We mitigated an infrastructure issue causing elevated latencies; engineers implemented routing limits and database connection pooling to stabilize services. If you see issues, contact support." happy to draft if you want.

support-bot: drafting customer note, will hold until final state confirmed.

incident-bot: pagerduty incident update: incident acknowledged by alex, status: mitigated -> monitoring.

maria (sre): relevant logs and commands used during mitigation (for runbook):
```
# Redis quick check
redis-cli -h redis-primary INFO clients | grep connected_clients
# Pgbouncer stats
echo "SHOW POOLS;" | psql pgbouncer://user@localhost:6432
# Postgres active connections
psql -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state='active';"
```

alex (oncall): will leave pgbouncer canary continuing and monitor for 30m. if stable, we'll complete rollout. Lee — you can take over at +40m if stable.

lee (next-oncall): copying steps. i'll watch metrics and be ready to roll back config if errors spike. please add a short checklist to the thread for the handoff.

alex (oncall): handoff checklist (short):
- verify error rate <= 2% and tail latency trending down
- pgbouncer canary success on 3 hosts (no increase in 5xx)
- redis clients <= 80% of maxclients on all primaries/replicas
- replication lag < 5s
- support message queued

sam (backend): can confirm canary reached 3 hosts, no regressions. queueing remainder of rollout in 5-min batches.

maria (sre): post-mortem notes to collect: root cause appears to be a job fanout amplification combined with many workers opening short-lived DB connections. remediation: enforce coalescing in enqueuer, use connection pooling (pgbouncer), and add DB-side connection exhaustion alerting tied to application-level rate limiting.

alex (oncall): handing off to lee now. I'm pausing active changes. leaving open pagerduty incident in monitoring state.

lee (next-oncall): ack handoff. i'll keep it open and watch for 1h then close if stable. thanks team. :white_check_mark: 

incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident status updated to 'resolved' by automation after 1h stable monitoring window. Incident closed. Reference: PROD-DB-CONN-CASCADE -> Postmortem required.

jess (product): thanks all — please link postmortem doc when ready and include customer-impact summary for comms.

support-bot: customer note posted to affected orgs (private). case numbers: #4531, #4532.

maria (sre): leaving this thread with recommended action items for postmortem and runbook updates:
- add automatic pgbouncer enablement path for heavy worker fleets
- add application-side enqueue de-duplication by default
- create synthetic tests for job-fanout patterns
- alert when redis `connected_clients` > 70% of maxclients for 5m

alex (oncall): final note: good teamwork. closing my active oncall tasks for this incident."
